subject: Dedicated capacity: autoscaling & queue sizing follow-up
thread_summary: Post-discovery follow-up covering SDK/auth, routing, structured output/tool-calling, embeddings/rerankers and dedicated capacity sizing (autoscaling, concurrency, queue depth). Agreed next step: technical deep-dive with Solutions Engineer on Jan 27 to validate queue thresholds and capacity plan.
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Helen Zhou <hzhou@shoplytics.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 24 Jan 2027 11:14:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity: autoscaling & queue sizing follow-up

Hi Helen — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call: 

Summary of what we covered:
- Integration & SDK: ShopLytics will use our Node + Python SDKs. Primary integration will be server-side (backend requests).
- Auth & network: customer requires VPC + mTLS to the inference plane and API key rotation. We discussed token rotation window and KMS options.
- Routing: route by region (US east primary) and latency SLO; fallback routing to smaller model variant during sustained saturation.
- Structured output & tool calling: you'll need tool-calling for enrichment (external DB lookups) and structured JSON outputs for downstream pipelines.
- Embeddings & rerankers: embedding calls from user actions (single-vector per action) and a separate reranker call in the scoring pipeline.

Dedicated capacity sizing notes (from our discussion):
- Peak sustained request rate: ~120 RPS (you mentioned spikes up to ~140)
- Avg request rate: ~80–95 RPS
- Median input length: ~60 tokens; some longer profiles up to 400 tokens for generate+context
- Concurrency per user flow: ~2–4 concurrent requests in bursts
- Embedding calls: ~30k/day (batchable)

Open questions we need to validate for sizing / autoscaling:
1) Confirm P95 latency target for chat/generate and embeddings.
2) Do you need strictly synchronous responses for the chat path or can you tolerate async for lower-priority flows?
3) Any regulatory constraints on cold-starts / instance reuse?

Proposed next step:
- Technical deep-dive with Aditya (solutions) to validate queue thresholds, autoscale triggers, and exact GPU pool sizing. Proposed times: Wed Jan 27 10:00 AM PT or 2:00 PM PT.

I attached a short architecture notes PDF and our dedicated checklist so Aditya can start a capacity calc. Please confirm the numbers above and which time works.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Peak sustained: 120 RPS, short spikes up to ~150 RPS (spikes last ~30–90s).
- Average: ~90 RPS during business hours, ~25 RPS off-peak.
- Typical token lengths: median 60 tokens for chat requests; up to 400 tokens for profile enrichment.
- Concurrency: most sessions create up to 3 concurrent calls; some automated flows briefly hit 6.
- Embeddings: ~30k embedding ops/day; we can batch these in a nightly window if helpful.

Latency targets: aiming for P95 <= 500ms for chat/generate; embeddings P95 <= 200ms.
We require single-tenant VPC for this pilot and would like mTLS + KMS-managed key rotation.

Wed Jan 27 at 10:00 AM PT works for a technical deep-dive. Looking forward to the capacity calc and recommendations.

—Helen

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Helen Zhou <hzhou@shoplytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Jan 2027 01:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: autoscaling & queue sizing follow-up

Thanks — planning notes ahead of Wed's deep-dive. I started a quick capacity calc (attached) and sketched recommended autoscale thresholds. Highlights: 

Capacity assumptions:
- Target P95 chat latency: 500ms (as Helen indicated). Embedding P95: 200ms.
- Based on median 60 tokens and batching behavior, an A100-equivalent GPU can sustain ~30–40 RPS for the primary chat model with 1k token window and dynamic batching. For your 120 RPS peak we recommend an initial pool of 4–6 GPUs to provide headroom / burst. If you want redundancy across availability zones we recommend 8 GPUs split across AZs.

Concurrency & queueing recommendations:
- Per-instance concurrency: limit to 8 active concurrent requests to avoid memory pressure; use an async queue for incoming requests to batch (continuous batching).
- Queue sizing: keep request queue target depth ~200 requests across the pool to allow batching to form; use a hard queue cap of 2000 to prevent uncontrolled backlog during outage.
- Autoscale policy (suggested): scale up +1 instance when average queue depth > 50 for 30s; scale up faster (+2) if queue > 200 for > 60s. Scale down when GPU utilization < 30% for 5 minutes and queue depth < 20.
- Burst capacity: configure reserved burst instances to absorb short spikes (we can reserve N instances for 5–10 minute bursts).

Other notes:
- KV cache: enable per-session KV cache to avoid re-encoding long contexts; this reduces per-request compute significantly for multi-turn flows.
- Routing: we can configure latency-based routing with automatic fallback to a smaller quantized model.
- Auth: mTLS + API token; we recommend short-lived tokens (1 hour) with automatic rotation via your KMS.
- Embeddings: batch nightly for large-scale indexing; for online embeddings keep a small async queue and provision 1–2 smaller CPU/GPU instances dedicated to embedding throughput with higher throughput per GPU for quantized models.

Questions for you before Wed:
1) Confirm AZ redundancy requirement (single AZ vs multi-AZ).
2) Any hard SLA for cold-starts / maximum cold-start time tolerated?
3) Will the reranker be on the same GPUs as chat or on a separate pool?

Attaching the quick capacity calc for review. I'll bring a rollout plan and expected cost delta for the recommended pool sizes to Wed's call.

-Aditya

Attachments:
- dedicated_capacity_capacity_calc.xlsx
